tools/pin_upload_port.py, a pre: script on every env, resolves the upload port from the board's own build.hwids and stops the build with the attached-port list rather than letting PlatformIO fall back to 'the best USB serial device'. Verified both paths on this machine (M4 on COM7, S3 absent) by temporarily widening the target gate so the same code ran under 'pio run -t buildprog': s3 refused, naming 239A:0125/8125/8126 + 303A:1001 and listing COM3/COM7; m4 resolved 'Upload port: COM7 (USB VID:PID=239A:80C9 ...)' and built. Not yet exercised through a real 'pio run -t upload' -- only the gate string differs. custom_upload_hwids=303A:1001 on the s3 envs covers ROM download mode, which the board definition does not list. Ports and VID:PIDs documented in docs/development.md ('Two boards on one USB bus'); pio device monitor cannot run build scripts, so that is documented as --port.

Fixed by 3.2's transport rewrite and verified on the M4, the board it was reported on. The old fetch read until the peer closed and then searched the buffer for CRLFCRLF; a close racing buffered bytes truncated the response so the search failed. readResponse() now reads the status line and headers with net::readLine, takes Content-Length and reads exactly that many bytes with net::readExactly -- there is no CRLFCRLF search left to fail.
